mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs and higher corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.5%, it signals a weakening labor market that typically prompts central bank intervention, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate policy support and reduced recession risk.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 7.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downward due to reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of robust industrial production growth (INDPRO annualized growth > 1.5%), the S&P 500 tends to deliver positive forward returns as corporate earnings growth is sustained, with the effect being most pronounced during early economic expansion phases when manufacturing activity drives overall economic momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO annualized growth > 1.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors price in sustained economic expansion and higher corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters with positive GDPC1 growth, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the annualized CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% signals rising inflation pressures that prompt the central bank to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as bond yields rise and equity valuations contract due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL annualized rate > 3.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a deteriorating labor market, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate hiring slowdowns and reduced consumer spending expectations weaken economic growth prospects.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative forward returns as manufacturing activity contraction signals weakening economic growth and corporate earnings, with the effect amplified during late-cycle phases when supply chain disruptions compound economic slowdowns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
